proposals.before: the second was the founding emperor, posthumously known as Emperor Wen;
proposals.after: the second was the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Wen;
proposals.reason: 太祖文皇帝 is Taizu (temple name) Emperor Wen, Gaozu's father—not himself the founding emperor.

proposals.before: Chongzhi rose to prominence through ability and resolve; his administration was notably stern, and he eventually reached the posts of General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Dongyang.
proposals.after: Chongzhi rose to prominence through ability and resolve; his administration was notably stern, and he eventually reached the posts of Champion General and Administrator of Dongyang.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, not 'General Who Establishes Might'.

proposals.before: When Gaozu took the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping with a fief of one thousand households and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief over North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
proposals.after: When Gaozu took the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping with a fief of one thousand households and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief over North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, Champion General, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, not 'General Who Establishes Might'.

decisions.reason: s0006 次太祖文皇帝 names Daoci’s second son by temple name 太祖 and posthumous title 文皇帝; he is Gaozu’s father, not the founding emperor, so the proposed idiomatic correctly removes that error.
s0019 官至冠軍將軍、東陽太守 gives the office 冠軍將軍, conventionally Champion General; “General Who Establishes Might” is a mistranslation, and the proposed idiomatic restores the correct title.
s0035 lists Jing’s continued offices as 冠軍將軍 among them; that title is Champion General, not “General Who Establishes Might,” and the proposed idiomatic corrects only that error.
